current_activity: 9th Panzer Division command post at Fresnay-sur-Sarthe came under fire from the U.S. XV Corps and withdrew north
notes: Event date: Breakout and Pursuit ch. 25 p. 498 puts the LXXXI Corps defending the le Mans-Alençon axis on 10 August with the 708th and 9th Panzer Divisions in line; p. 500: the command posts of the 9th Panzer and Panzer Lehr Divisions at Fresnay-sur-Sarthe came under fire, and both units withdrew to the north. Location: Fresnay-sur-Sarthe is named for the command post. Opponents: the two armored divisions of the U.S. XV Corps jumped off abreast; the 9th Panzer and 352d Divisions together claimed thirty-six tanks.

current_activity: Brandenberger relieves the commander and the chief of staff of the 9th Panzer Division in the Stolberg Corridor
notes: Event date: CMH Siegfried Line Campaign ch. 4 p. 87: "As of nightfall, 16 September, the division lacked even a commander. Visiting the division command post, the Seventh Army commander, General Brandenberger, charged that General Mueller was unaware of the actual situation on his front. He relieved both Mueller and Mueller's chief of staff.". Event definition: the relief of General Mueller as of 16 September; the successor is not named in the passage. Event support: one source family (CMH). Location: Stolberg, the town at the head of the Stolberg Corridor where the division held the front, with a precision of 10 km. Location approximate: a sector point; the division command post is not named. Location support: CMH names the Stolberg Corridor. Commander: unknown. Opponents: US VII Corps (3rd Armored Division).
